samples.summary: Gate 1b's pagination is never exercised — the stub cannot even express a second page, so a reader that only ever looks at page 1 passes the whole suite
samples.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` (mark-ready.mjs:181-195) loops up to 10 pages, continues while `files.length === 100`, and throws (fail-closed) past 1000 files. The stub's files branch is `page === 1 ? cfg.files || [] : []` (mark-ready.test.mjs:79-83), and every fixture in the new gate-1b test (lines 269-298) supplies 1-item single pages, so `files.length < 100` returns on page 1 in every run. Nothing asserts that a workflow edit appearing only on page 2+ is caught, and nothing asserts the >1000-file `throw` reaches the fail-closed exit-1 path. Delete the loop and keep only page 1, or invert the `< 100` continuation, and all tests still pass — while an `agent:managed` PR with >100 changed files that guts `.github/workflows/ci.yml` would auto-promote on its own gutted CI run, which is exactly the attack gate 1b is advertised to close. Searched mark-ready.test.mjs for `page=`, `per_page`, `1000 changed files` (one hit, in the stub itself).

samples.summary: The `unexpected response from the PR files endpoint` guard (non-array response) has no test
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs:184 throws when the files endpoint returns a non-array (e.g. `{ "message": "Not Found" }`, which the real API serves with a 200-shaped body via `gh` in some error modes). The stub's files branch always writes a JSON array (mark-ready.test.mjs:79-83) and no fixture makes it return an object, so the guard — which is what stops a malformed body from being treated as 'no files changed', i.e. gate 1b passing — is unexecuted by the suite. The `fail:` mechanism only covers a non-zero `gh` exit, a different path.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. mark-ready.mjs:182-194 paginates pulls/{n}/files up to 10 pages, continues while files.length === 100, and throws (fail-closed via ranBaseCiDefinition, mark-ready.mjs:197-208) past 1000 files. The test stub's files branch (mark-ready.test.mjs:79-83) returns cfg.files only for page 1 and [] for every later page, so it cannot express a second page at all; every gate-1b fixture (mark-ready.test.mjs:113, 269-298) is a single-element file list, so the loop always returns on page 1 with files.length < 100. Consequently a workflow edit visible only on page 2+, and the >1000-file throw reaching the exit-1 fail-closed path, are both unasserted — deleting the loop or inverting the `< 100` continuation leaves the whole suite green. I searched wide for a counterexample: every *.test.mjs referencing mark-ready.mjs (only this file spawns the CLI; checks.test.mjs:537-549 merely greps its source for workflow-file scoping), and repo-wide greps for page=2 / paginat / per_page=100&page / 1000 changed files / CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES / gate 1b. No test anywhere exercises the pagination or the >1000-file refusal. Blocking under this lens: gate 1b is a new guard whose failure silently auto-promotes an agent:managed PR that gutted .github/workflows/ci.yml, i.e. a silently weakened guard (major).

finding.summary: Gate 1's identity check lost all behavioral coverage; the process-level stub was loosened so a regression to the unscoped query would keep the suite green
finding.evidence: This delta deletes the three process-level tests that proved gate 1 rejects a forged/foreign workflow run ("gate 1 reads the CI WORKFLOW FILE", "gate 1 is not forgeable by a SECOND workflow file…", and the @ref test) and simultaneously removes the `path` filter from `ciConclusion` (checks.mjs:117 now does `newestRun(workflowRuns || [])`). The whole identity guarantee now rests on the URL mark-ready sends, but the stub `gh` matches any api call containing `/runs?head_sha=` (mark-ready.test.mjs:67) and returns the fixture regardless — so nothing in mark-ready.test.mjs observes which URL was requested, even though `calls`/`tokenCalls` already record it. If mark-ready.mjs reverted to `repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=…`, every process-level test still passes AND a forged newest run would now be accepted, because ciConclusion no longer filters. The only remaining defense is the source-text grep in checks.test.mjs:537-549, i.e. a regex over the file rather than an observation of behavior. A one-line `assert.match(calls.find(c=>c.startsWith("api")), /actions\/workflows\/ci\.yml\/runs/)` would restore behavioral coverage of the guard this whole change exists to strengthen.

verdict.reason: The tests the finding says were deleted are present and behavioral. scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:207-260 runs mark-ready as a process against a stub gh that serves BOTH endpoints the way GitHub does: the scoped branch (line 67 matches only "actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=", contradicting the finding's claim that it matches any "/runs?head_sha=") and the unscoped branch (lines 71-78) which returns otherRuns — including a forged run with path .github/workflows/pwn.yml, name "CI", conclusion success and the highest id — concatenated with workflowRuns. Because ciConclusion (checks.mjs:116-119) picks the newest run without a path filter, a regression of mark-ready.mjs to the unscoped URL would be handed that forged green run and would promote, breaking the assertions at lines 236-241 (code === 1, !promoted). So a revert would NOT keep the suite green. Furthermore the exact assertion the finding proposes as missing already exists: lines 245-254 collect calls starting with "api " containing head_sha=, assert at least one, then assert.match(/actions\/workflows\/ci\.yml\/runs\?head_sha=cafe7/) and assert.doesNotMatch(/actions\/runs\?/). Line 257-259 also pins the positive direction (CI green amid the noise promotes). The claim that the only remaining defense is a source-text grep in checks.test.mjs is therefore false.
